Present one open decision or one step at a time, not a full survey of every issue at once. Skip
spec nitpicks that don't block the current step. Design decisions get written up as they are made,
as many small ones as needed, in the course's four-field format (Decision / Alternatives
Considered / Rationale / Consequences), appended to `.specstory/issue-<N>-design-decisions.md`
(gitignored) for the user to paste into the issue.

Write decisions in plain language, not implementation detail: what was chosen and what it means for
users and developers, few identifiers or signatures, no test-harness internals. The user posts them
per commit as issue comments headed `# Design Decision for the <Nth> commit (<what it did>)`, with
decisions numbered across the issue. Model: their comments on #53 and #54 (2026-10-18 feedback on
#56: "they should not be that implementation heavy").

**Why:** on 2026-09-27 the first plan for issue #53 listed spec fixes, two design choices, AC
ambiguities and a six-commit plan in one reply; the user said "no need to be *that* pedantic. One
at a time."

**How to apply:** keep the careful detail-checking, but surface only what the current step needs.

=== user-makes-every-commit.md
---
name: user-makes-every-commit
description: "Never run git commit, even with approval; propose small commits and let them commit"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: a96225c0-b3ad-4c78-bedc-ff767c9a0397
  modified: 2026-09-27T20:02:09.436Z
---

Never run `git commit` (or amend, stage-and-commit, etc.) on this user's behalf — not even after
they approve the change. Stricter than `AGENTS.md`, which allows a commit once a human approves it.
Plan work as a sequence of small commits, each doing one thing; for each, say which files changed
and why, give a draft Conventional Commit message with the `(#N)` suffix and `Assisted-by` trailer,
and stop so they can review and commit it themselves.

**Why:** stated as a baseline rule on 2026-09-27 ("You CANNOT commit on my behalf, ever"). They
want to understand every change they land, and they don't want time-pressure detours.

The draft message is only a suggestion: they write their own, deliberately brief (upstream squashes
on merge), and said not to review or correct it afterwards (2026-09-27, issue #53).

"Small commits" is for code, where commits guard against breaking changes. Docs-only changes
(`.claude-students/` pages and guides) go in one commit together, not split per doc.

**How to apply:** after each step, stop at "ready for you to commit" with the draft message. Keep
changes careful, catch easy-to-miss details, and flag when `.claude-students` docs need updating
alongside the code. Related: [[teach-through-navigation]], [[review-dont-fix-student-prs]].

Explain *where* and *why* before *what*. Name the discovery method — which grep, which doc, which
file answered the question — not just the conclusion. Then give exact edits for the user to type
themselves, and verify afterwards with the repo's own tooling.

**Why:** this is coursework (CSCI435). The deliverable is the skill of navigating an unfamiliar
large codebase; the diff is a by-product. A correct patch handed over teaches nothing.

**How to apply:** start from the user-visible page and work backwards (URL → route → handler →
template → the element). Prefer one generic mechanism over repeated edits across pages, and say why.
Offer to draft prose (docs, PR text) rather than code. Keep it moving — they have said more than
once they do not want to spend hours. See [[evidence-over-assertion]] and
[[prefers-make-targets]].

For graded writing that is meant to show their own understanding (D6 diagram Q&A, D7 check-in),
offer the facts as bullets, not finished answers. They deliberately write it lighter on detail than
the facts given, so it reflects what they actually understand and can recall. When asked to check
it, fix spelling, formatting and sentence structure, and correct only factual errors, explaining
each one. Keep their voice and level of detail, and don't add points they left out.

**Why:** the user, 2026-10-18 (issue #56 Q&A): "I could copy what you told me, but it does not truly
represent what I understand, and so I kept it a little lighter on details that make it easier for
me to learn and recollect."

**How to apply:** note any factual corrections separately from the wording changes. Related:
[[teach-through-navigation]], [[one-step-at-a-time]].
=== review-dont-fix-student-prs.md
---
name: review-dont-fix-student-prs
description: "On student PRs: report findings, never offer to apply the fixes"
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

When reviewing a student's PR, hand back the findings and stop. Do not offer to reword the commit,
add the missing trailer, or apply the cleanups — the student makes each change themselves, one
change per commit.

**Why:** CSCI435 coursework. Landing several concerns in one commit is the habit being corrected;
a commit that does one thing would have exposed its own missing details at review time. Fixing it
for them removes both lessons. Same principle as [[teach-through-navigation]].

**How to apply:** name each finding with its `file:line` and say which rule or neighbouring code it
conflicts with, so the student can act on it unaided. Verify with the repo's own tooling
(see [[prefers-make-targets]]) and report what passed. End the review at the findings — no "want me
to stage it?".

{"body":"Closes #56\n\n## What changed and why\n\nGitea's keyboard shortcuts were one page-wide key handler that searched the page for a `<kbd>` hint showing the pressed key and focused the box beside it. That only allowed \"press a letter to focus a box\": no two-key sequences, no shortcut without a box, and nothing could list the shortcuts for a help dialog. This PR replaces it with one place to add shortcuts. Nothing changes for the user and `s` and `t` work as before.\n\n- **One call to add a shortcut:** `registerShortcut()` takes the keys, a translated description, an optional section and the action to run. `getShortcuts()` lists the shortcuts on the current page, for the help dialog in #57.\n- **Two-key sequences** such as `g c`: the second key must come within 1500 ms. Pressing `g` does nothing else while it waits, and a key that doesn't finish a sequence counts as a fresh press.\n- **Shortcuts stay out of the way:** nothing runs while typing in a field, while Ctrl, Alt or Cmd is held, or when a widget such as a menu has already used the key. Holding a key down runs its shortcut once.\n- **Clashes fail loudly:** adding the same keys twice, or keys where one starts the other (a lone `g` and `g c`), throws an error instead of one silently winning.\n- **A shortcut can belong to part of the page,** and only exists while that part is on the page. This is what lets the `T` hint come back after moving through the file tree, which swaps the page content, without counting as a clash.\n- **The `S` and `T` hints register themselves** through the new code. Each is listed with its box's placeholder (\"Search code…\", \"Go to file\") and the existing \"Repository\" string as its section, so no new string was needed.\n- The docs in `.claude-students` are updated with additions and corrections from this implementation\n\n## How the changes relate to the ACs\n\n- **AC1:** `s` on a repository home page focuses the code search box and hides its hint; `t` does the same for \"Go to file\" on file and folder views.\n- **AC2:** Escape in a box with a hint clears it and moves focus away, as before.\n- **AC3:** a single-key shortcut such as `?` runs once, and the key does nothing else.\n- **AC4:** `g` then `c` within 1500 ms runs the sequence once, and neither key runs a shortcut of its own.\n- **AC5:** after more than 1500 ms, or after a key that doesn't finish any sequence, the `g` is dropped and the next key is a fresh press.\n- **AC6:** keys typed into an input, textarea, select or editable area run no shortcut and type as normal.\n- **AC7:** a key a widget has already used runs no shortcut and drops a half-typed sequence.\n- **AC8:** adding the same keys again, or keys where one starts the other, throws; a hint that loads again after file-tree navigation is not an error, and its key keeps working.\n- **AC9:** each listed shortcut has its keys, description and, if given, section; `s` and `t` use their box's placeholder and are in the Repository section.\n\n## How it was tested\n\n### Test strategy\n\nThere were no tests for keyboard shortcuts before this PR, so every test here is new.\n\n- **Unit tests (Vitest) for the logic.** Most of the changes related to rules about which key presses run which shortcut. These need no server, so they are tested on their own with a fake clock so the timeout tests don't have to wait. The registry tests each build their own list of shortcuts, and the hint tests clear the page after each test, so no test leaks into another. 19 tests in `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.test.ts`.\n- **Playwright tests for the wiring.** The `S` and `T` hints only work once Gitea's templates, the Vue \"Go to file\" box and the page setup code have all run, and none of that exists in a unit test. Three tests in tests/e2e/shortcut.test.ts drive real pages for what depends on that wiring: the hints (AC1, AC2, AC6, AC9), a key the language menu uses (AC7) and the file tree (AC8).\n\n**Testing the tests.** Mutation testing performed during implementation of tests to ensure they actually catch the intended errors. Each break made the matching test fail, so the tests check the behaviour and don't just run. The final review found two checks no test reached (Shift pressed in the middle of a sequence, and the key of a removed element), and tests were added for both.\n\n**Not covered automatically, and why.** AC3, AC4 and AC5 have no real-page test, because no page has a sequence or a `?` shortcut yet; they get one when #57 and #58 add them.\n\n**Checked by hand.** Claude also drove a headless browser through a local instance, and I had a look to ensure the changes actually did not change visible/user facing behavior.\n\n**Misc.** Token heavy review workflow with reviewers and critics was run at the end to ensure things were not overlooked. It found that holding a key down ran its shortcut again, which is now fixed and tested.\n\n| AC | What the tests check |\n| --- | --- |\n| AC1 | Pressing `s` and `t` focuses each box and hides its hint, in the unit tests and on a real repository page |\n| AC2 | Escape clears the box, moves focus away and brings the hint back, in both |\n| AC3 | A single key runs its action once and is used up; an unregistered key is left alone; case doesn't matter; holding a key down runs it once |\n| AC4 | `g c` within 1500 ms runs once, and a single-key `c` doesn't run, even when `c` is held or Shift is pressed in between |\n| AC5 | Waiting past 1500 ms, or pressing a key that finishes no sequence, drops the `g` and treats the key as a fresh press |\n| AC6 | Input, textarea, select and editable areas run nothing; typing into a field drops a half-typed sequence; on a real page, typing `st` in the search box just types |\n| AC7 | A key a widget already used runs nothing and drops a half-typed sequence; Ctrl, Alt and Cmd presses run nothing; on a real page, `s` in the language menu jumps to a language and the search box stays unfocused |\n| AC8 | Duplicate and overlapping keys throw; a shortcut whose element left the page stops working and gives way to a new one; on a real page, `t` still works after moving through the file tree twice |\n| AC9 | The list gives keys, description and section, and drops a shortcut whose element left the page; a hint is listed with its box's placeholder and section; the real hints carry the Repository section |\n\n## CI / manual verification\n\n- CI runs on the PR; per the course rules, it must pass before merging.\n- `make test-frontend`: 356 tests pass, including the 19 new ones.\n- `make lint-js`, `make lint-templates` and `make lint-editorconfig` pass.\n- The 3 Playwright tests pass locally on Chromium and Firefox.\n\n## Design\n\nDesign decisions noted under issue #56.\n\n## Tech Debt\n\n**Introduced:**\n- A shortcut tied to an element counts as present while the element is on the page, even when it is hidden. That is enough for the `S` and `T` hints, but #58 and #59, whose shortcuts should only work while their tab or button is shown, will have to tie them to something that is removed or check visibility themselves. In other words, any shortcuts need to tie themselves to an element with the same lifetime, so they stop working when it goes and can register again without a clash.\n- If an element is taken off the page and the same element is put back, its shortcut can be lost for good: registering any other shortcut in between clears out shortcuts whose element is gone, and Gitea never sets up the same element twice. No current page does this (the file tree creates new elements), but #58 and #59 should not move their elements around.\n\n**Encountered:**\n- Moving through the file tree swaps the page content but never unmounts the Vue \"Go to file\" box inside it, so each move leaves one detached copy behind. Handled by not relying on cleanup: a shortcut tied to an element that has left the page is replaced when its hint registers again. Not fixed here.\n- Gitea's page setup (`data-global-init`) has no error isolation: if one element's setup throws while the page loads, every element after it is left unset, and content added to the page later is never set up either, because the watcher for new content never starts. A second hint for the same key now throws there (AC8), so that mistake would break the rest of the page's setup. This follows the existing pattern, as setup already throws on other developer mistakes such as a misspelled function name. Not fixed here.\n\n## AI assistance\n\nClaude Code (claude-opus-5-5) drafted the code, tests, docs and other changes, ran the headless-browser checks and an automated review. I made the decisions, refused to let Claude commit on my behalf, and made commits as small as possible so I could review each one with its tests. {"assignees":["controlled-opposition"],"body":"\u003e Sub-issue of #23 · **P1** · estimate **5 points** (medium) · blocked by #56\n\n## User Story\nAs a keyboard user who suspects Gitea has shortcuts but cannot find them, I want to press `?` on any page and see the shortcuts that work on that page, grouped by section, so that I can learn them without reading the source or the docs.\n\n## User Scenario\nA user is on a repository's home page and presses `?`. A dialog titled \"Keyboard shortcuts\" opens in the middle of the page. It lists `?` under \"General\". It lists `S` (\"Search code…\") and `T` (\"Go to file\") under \"Repository\". Each row shows the keys as `\u003ckbd\u003e` elements next to the description. Focus moves into the dialog, and Tab never reaches the page behind it. The user presses Escape. The dialog closes, and focus returns to where it was.\n\nOn the notifications page, no shortcuts belong to the page itself. There, `?` opens the same dialog and lists only `?`.\n\n## Acceptance Criteria\n- [ ] AC1: Given any page that loads Gitea's main script, and focus outside a text field, when the user presses `?`, then a dialog titled \"Keyboard shortcuts\" opens. It has one row for each shortcut that #56's `getShortcuts()` returns on that page, with the shortcut's keys and description.\n- [ ] AC2: Given the dialog is open, when the user presses Escape, then the dialog closes and focus returns to the element that had focus before the dialog opened.\n- [ ] AC3: Given the dialog is open, when the user presses Tab repeatedly, then focus never reaches a control on the page behind the dialog.\n- [ ] AC4: Given focus is in an input, a textarea or an editable area, when the user types `?`, then a `?` character appears in the field and the dialog does not open.\n- [ ] AC5: Given shortcuts with different section labels, when the dialog opens, then each section is a heading with its shortcuts under it. A shortcut that later code registers with a new section appears under that section, with no change to the dialog's code.\n- [ ] AC6: Given a page in a language other than English, when the dialog opens, then the title, the close button's accessible name and the \"General\" heading come from locale keys.\n- [ ] AC7: Given the dialog is open, when the user presses `?` again, then the dialog stays open and unchanged, and no error occurs.\n- [ ] AC8: Given the dialog is open, when the user presses the key of another shortcut on the page, then that shortcut does not run. For example, `s` on a repository home page does not move focus to the code search box.\n- [ ] AC9: A Playwright test in `tests/e2e/` covers AC1, AC2, AC4 and AC8 on a repository home page and calls `assertNoJsError`. Unit tests in `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.test.ts` cover the grouping in AC5.\n\n## Out of Scope\n- Shortcuts other than `?`. The `g` shortcuts are #58, `c` is #59, and `r` is #95. Each one appears in the dialog when its issue registers it.\n- Shortcuts that belong to other pages. The dialog lists only what works on the current page.\n- Editing or remapping a shortcut from the dialog.\n- The setting that turns shortcuts off. #60 adds that setting to this dialog as a checkbox.\n- A link to the dialog in the footer or in a menu.\n- A printable list or a documentation page of shortcuts.\n\n## Open Questions\n- Should the user also be able to open the dialog with the mouse, for example from a footer link? Proposed: not in this issue. One way in keeps the e2e test complete.\n- Should a click on the backdrop close the dialog? Proposed: no. Escape and the close button are then the only ways out. Reviewer to confirm.\n\n## Design Decision\n\n### Decision 1: build the dialog on the native `\u003cdialog\u003e` element\n**Decision:** Build the dialog on the native `\u003cdialog\u003e` element and open it with `showModal()`.\n\n**Alternatives Considered:**\n- (a) A Fomantic modal that `showFomanticModal` in `web_src/js/modules/fomantic/modal.ts` opens. Gitea's other modals use this today.\n- (b) A plain `\u003cdiv\u003e` with a focus trap, a backdrop and an Escape handler written by hand.\n\n**Rationale:** `.claude-students/docs/frontend-js.md` says Fomantic is deprecated and that new features must not use it. Sibling issue #25 exists to remove Fomantic from the accessibility path, so a new Fomantic modal in an accessibility feature works against #25. `showModal()` makes the page behind the dialog inert (AC3), closes the dialog on Escape (AC2) and sets `aria-modal`. Option (b) would rewrite behaviour that the browser already has, and hand-written focus handling causes the kind of bug that #25 fixes.\n\n**Consequences:** The browser provides most of AC2 and AC3, and the dialog needs no jQuery. Browsers differ on where focus goes when a dialog closes, so the close handler restores focus itself. #56's registry listens to key presses on the whole document, so the dialog must stop other shortcuts while it is open (AC8). This is the first native `\u003cdialog\u003e` in Gitea. No shared helper exists, and the dialog needs its own CSS to match `web_src/css/modules/modal.css`.\n\n### Decision 2: render the dialog's markup and text on the server\n**Decision:** Render the empty `\u003cdialog\u003e` once in the base page template, next to the footer script, and keep it hidden until it opens. The server renders the translated title, close label and \"General\" heading. When the user presses `?`, JavaScript adds the rows from `getShortcuts()`.\n\n**Alternatives Considered:**\n- (a) Build the whole dialog in JavaScript, and add its strings to `window.config.i18n` in `templates/base/head_script.tmpl`.\n- (b) A Vue component that mounts on demand and receives its strings as `data-locale-*` attributes.\n\n**Rationale:** The #56 registry already receives its descriptions and section labels as text that the server translated into the page. A dialog that the server renders follows the same pattern. Option (a) is possible, because `templates/base/head_script.tmpl` allows general texts in `window.config.i18n`. But (a) splits the dialog's text between two mechanisms, and it builds markup in JavaScript that the template can hold. Option (b) adds a component and a mount for a static list. `.claude-students/docs/frontend-vue-components.md` advises against Vue for markup this simple.\n\n**Consequences:** Every page carries a few hundred bytes of hidden markup. The `s` and `t` shortcuts register from a `\u003ckbd\u003e` hint on the page, but `?` has no hint. JavaScript registers `?` instead, and reads its description and \"General\" label from data attributes on the dialog.\n\n## Scope\nmedium (5 points)\n\n---\n*Spec refined with Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5), reviewed and posted by @controlled-opposition.*\n","comments":[{"author":"ab-wm","body":"Spec reviewed: \nI do not see anything wrong with the specs, though do note that claude-students documentation are as accurate as they can, but can be incorrect in the finer details."}],"state":"OPEN","title":"`?` opens a shortcut help dialog built from the registry"}

```text
Exit code 1
import {registerGlobalInitFunc} from './observer.ts';
import {hideElem, toggleElem} from '../utils/dom.ts';

const sequenceTimeoutMs = 1500; // the longest wait between the keys of a sequence

export type Shortcut = {
  keys: string, // keys pressed one after another, separated by spaces, e.g. "g c"
  description: string, // translated
  section?: string, // translated
  element?: HTMLElement, // the shortcut only exists while this element is in the document
  action: () => void,
};

export type ShortcutInfo = Pick<Shortcut, 'keys' | 'description' | 'section'>;

function isActive(shortcut: Shortcut): boolean {
  return !shortcut.element || shortcut.element.isConnected;
}

// returns the shortcut for exactly these keys, 'prefix' if they start a longer sequence, or null
function matchKeys(shortcuts: Shortcut[], keys: string): Shortcut | 'prefix' | null {
  for (const shortcut of shortcuts) {
    if (shortcut.keys === keys) return shortcut;
    if (shortcut.keys.startsWith(`${keys} `)) return 'prefix';
  }
  return null;
}

export class ShortcutRegistry {
  shortcuts: Shortcut[] = [];
  pendingKeys = ''; // the start of a sequence pressed so far
  pendingTime = 0;

  register(shortcut: Shortcut) {
    const keys = shortcut.keys.toLowerCase();
    // a shortcut whose element has left the page, e.g. a hint replaced by file tree navigation, gives way to the new one
    this.shortcuts = this.shortcuts.filter(isActive);
    const conflict = this.shortcuts.find((s) => s.keys === keys || s.keys.startsWith(`${keys} `) || keys.startsWith(`${s.keys} `));
    if (conflict) throw new Error(`Keyboard shortcut "${keys}" conflicts with "${conflict.keys}"`);
    this.shortcuts.push({...shortcut, keys});
  }

  list(): ShortcutInfo[] {
    return this.shortcuts.filter(isActive).map(({keys, description, section}) => ({keys, description, section}));
  }

  handleKeyDown(e: KeyboardEvent) {
    const target = e.target as HTMLElement;
    // the key was already used by a widget such as a menu, or is being typed into a field
    if (e.defaultPrevented || e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey || e.altKey || target.matches('input, textarea, select') || target.isContentEditable) {
      this.pendingKeys = '';
      return;
    }
    if (e.key === 'Shift') return; // not a press of its own, e.g. on the way to "?"
    if (e.repeat) return; // a held key runs its shortcut once, and doesn't start over after a sequence

    if (Date.now() - this.pendingTime > sequenceTimeoutMs) this.pendingKeys = '';
    const key = e.key.toLowerCase();
    const shortcuts = this.shortcuts.filter(isActive);
    let keys = this.pendingKeys ? `${this.pendingKeys} ${key}` : key;
    let match = matchKeys(shortcuts, keys);
    if (!match && keys !== key) {
      // the key does not continue the sequence, so it acts as a fresh press
      keys = key;
      match = matchKeys(shortcuts, keys);
    }
    this.pendingKeys = '';
    if (!match) return;

    e.preventDefault();
    if (match === 'prefix') {
      this.pendingKeys = keys;
      this.pendingTime = Date.now();
    } else {
      match.action();
    }
  }
}

const globalRegistry = new ShortcutRegistry();

// Adds a keyboard shortcut to the page. Throws if the keys clash with an existing shortcut.
export function registerShortcut(shortcut: Shortcut) {
  globalRegistry.register(shortcut);
}

// The shortcuts available on the current page, e.g. for a help dialog
export function getShortcuts(): ShortcutInfo[] {
  return globalRegistry.list();
}

export function initShortcutKbd(kbd: HTMLElement) {
  // Handle initial state: hide the kbd hint if the associated input already has a value
  // (e.g., from browser autofill or back/forward navigation cache)
  const elem = elemFromKbd(kbd)!;
  if (elem.value) hideElem(kbd);
  kbd.setAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true');
  kbd.setAttribute('aria-keyshortcuts', kbd.getAttribute('data-shortcut-keys')!);
  registerShortcut({
    keys: kbd.getAttribute('data-shortcut-keys')!,
    description: elem.placeholder,
    section: kbd.getAttribute('data-shortcut-section') ?? undefined,
    element: kbd,
    action: () => elem.focus(),
  });
}

function shortcutWrapper(el: HTMLElement): HTMLElement | null {
  const parent = el.parentElement;
  return parent?.matches('.global-shortcut-wrapper') ? parent : null;
}

function elemFromKbd(kbd: HTMLElement): HTMLInputElement | HTMLTextAreaElement | null {
  return shortcutWrapper(kbd)?.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('input, textarea') || null;
}

function kbdFromElem(input: HTMLElement): HTMLElement | null {
  return shortcutWrapper(input)?.querySelector<HTMLElement>('kbd') || null;
}

export function initGlobalShortcut() {
  registerGlobalInitFunc('onGlobalShortcut', initShortcutKbd);
  document.addEventListener('keydown', (e: KeyboardEvent) => globalRegistry.handleKeyDown(e));

  // A <kbd> element next to an <input> declares a keyboard shortcut for that input.
  // When the matching key is pressed, the sibling input is focused.
  // When Escape is pressed inside such an input, the input is cleared and blurred.
  // The <kbd> element is shown/hidden automatically based on input focus and value.
  document.addEventListener('keydown', (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
    // Modifier keys are not supported yet
    if (e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey || e.altKey) return;

    const target = e.target as HTMLElement;

    // Handle Escape: clear and blur inputs that have an associated keyboard shortcut
    if (e.key === 'Escape') {
      const kbd = kbdFromElem(target);
      if (kbd) {
        (target as HTMLInputElement).value = '';
        (target as HTMLInputElement).blur();
      }
    }
  });

  // Toggle kbd shortcut hint visibility on input focus/blur
  document.addEventListener('focusin', (e) => {
    const kbd = kbdFromElem(e.target as HTMLElement);
    if (!kbd) return;
    hideElem(kbd);
  });

  document.addEventListener('focusout', (e) => {
    const kbd = kbdFromElem(e.target as HTMLElement);
    if (!kbd) return;
    const hasContent = Boolean((e.target as HTMLInputElement).value);
    toggleElem(kbd, !hasContent);
  });
}

```text
# Course workflow — issues, PRs, reviews, sprint deliverables

Course rules, not upstream Gitea ones. Source: the course site <https://csci-435-se.github.io/>
(Sprints pages) and `docs/sprint0/standards.md`. Everyone on the team, and every AI session, uses
the formats below so all issues and PRs look the same. The GitHub templates in `.github/` carry the
same formats; if they ever disagree with this page, fix the template.

AI disclosure has its own page: `AI-ASSISTANCE.md`.

## Current sprint: Sprint 2

- **Dates:** Oct 13 – Oct 29, 2026. Everything pushed and merged by **Oct 29, 11:59 PM**, except
  the D7 check-in, due **Oct 22, 11:59 PM**.
- **Points:** 100.
- **Zero rule:** no merged PR (D4), no sprint report (D8) or no release (D9) means **0 for the
  whole sprint**.
- **Carries forward:** anything the Sprint 2 page doesn't change comes from the Sprint 1 page, and
  every Sprint 0 standard still applies.

| # | Deliverable | Points | Who | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D1 | Sprint backlog: a `Sprint 2` milestone with every selected issue on it | 10 | Team | GitHub milestone |
| D2 | Requirements spec for each issue (formats below), peer-reviewed by a teammate before coding | 20 | Individual | Issue body |
| D3 | At least one non-trivial design decision per issue, with **at least two alternatives** | 5 | Individual | Issue body |
| D4 | Code changes and PRs, each with a `## Tech Debt` section | 20 | Individual | PRs |
| D5 | AI logs | 5 | Individual | `ai-logs/sprint2/<github-username>/` |
| D6 | UML class and sequence diagrams plus Q&A for one medium issue you resolved | 15 | Individual | `docs/sprint2/diagrams/` |
| D7 | Mid-sprint check-in | 5 | Individual | `docs/sprint2/checkin/<github-username>.md` |
| D8 | Sprint report | 10 | Team | `docs/sprint2/report.md` |
| D9 | Release: tag `v1.27.3-csci435-s2` plus a GitHub release | 2 | Team | Tags / Releases |
| D10 | Reflection survey | 8 | Individual | Blackboard/Zulip link |

- **D1 load:** each CSCI 435 student owns at least 2 medium issues; each CSCI 535 student owns at
  least 2 medium and 1 small. Either load can be met with equivalent story points instead. Every
  issue has exactly **one** assignee. Unfinished Sprint 1 issues
  go into the backlog before new work. To skip one, write the reason on that issue (closed, made
  invalid by later changes, or no longer relevant).
- **D3:** each decision names at least two concrete alternatives and why one won; this is graded
  strictly. The site also accepts the decision in an issue comment or the PR description; the team
  keeps it in the issue body. Decisions that span issues go in `docs/sprint2/design.md`.
- **D4:** every PR description has the Tech Debt section (see "Pull request format"). A PR without
  it loses points.
- **D5:** conventions are in `ai-logs/README.md`. Logs hold the full prompts and output: summaries,
  screenshots and share links are not logs. The link must open the log file itself, not a folder or
  another issue. The folder must exist even if no AI was used; in that case, post a comment saying
  so. The site accepts the link in an issue or a PR comment this sprint; the team keeps it in
  **issue comments only** (`AI-ASSISTANCE.md`).
- **D6:** see "UML diagrams (D6)" below.
- **D7:** about 150 words on each of: what you have done and what remains; one thing you learned
  about the codebase or about software engineering; one thing you would do differently. Late or
  thin scores 3 of 5.
- **D9:** keep the base version (`v1.27.3-csci435-s1` → `v1.27.3-csci435-s2`), tag after every
  Sprint 2 PR is merged, push the tag to origin, and write release notes listing the features,
  fixes and improvements. The site's example says `v2.17.2`; this fork's base is `v1.27.3`.
- **Reviews:** nobody approves or merges their own PR. Reviewers leave substantive comments, not a
  bare approval. Tell the reviewer on Zulip or by email, and aim to review within 24 hours. Each
  student reviews at least one PR per sprint, and every teammate at least once per semester.
- **Extra credit:** up to 3 points per PR accepted by upstream Gitea.

## Branches and commits

- Branches: `feat/issue-<N>-short-description`, `fix/issue-<N>-short-description` or
  `chore/short-description` (`STUDENTS.md`). One issue per branch.
- Commit messages follow Conventional Commits and end with the issue number:
  `feat(repo): show empty state on releases page (#17)`. Add an
  `Assisted-by: AGENT_NAME:MODEL_VERSION` trailer when AI helped; never `Co-Authored-By` or
  `Signed-off-by` (`AGENTS.md`). A human approves every commit before it is made.

### Before each implementation: sync with main

Every new branch starts from an up-to-date `main`. AI sessions run this before writing any code:

```bash
git switch main
git pull origin main
git switch -c feat/issue-<N>-short-description
```

To pick up new work on `main` for a branch that already exists, **merge, don't rebase**. Rebasing
or squashing after review has started is not allowed (`docs/sprint0/standards.md`):

```bash
git fetch origin
git merge origin/main
```

Do this before opening the PR and again if `main` moves while it is in review. Never merge another
feature branch into yours.

### After merge: clean up

A PR is merged with a merge commit once it is approved, every review comment is addressed and CI
passes. Then:

```bash
git switch main
git pull origin main
git branch -d feat/issue-<N>-short-description               # local branch
git push origin --delete feat/issue-<N>-short-description    # or GitHub's "Delete branch" button
git fetch --prune                                            # drop stale remote-tracking refs
```

Also check that the issue closed (via `Closes #N`), is on the sprint milestone, and has its AI
Assistance comment. Then run `specstory sync` and file the session's log (see `ai-logs/README.md`).

## Issue format: feature (user story)

Template: `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/user-story.yaml`. The user story must meet INVEST: Independent,
Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, Testable.

```markdown
## User Story
As a <role>, I want <capability> so that <benefit>.

## User Scenario
<A short concrete walk-through: who, where in the UI, what they do, what they see.>

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given <state>, when <action>, then <observable result>.
- [ ] AC2: ...
- [ ] AC3: ...            (at least 3; each has a clear pass/fail result)

## Out of Scope
- <What this issue deliberately does not do.>

## Open Questions
- <Unresolved questions, or "None".>

## Design Decision
**Decision:** <what was chosen>
**Alternatives Considered:** <at least two concrete options, and why each lost>
**Rationale:** <why this one>
**Consequences:** <trade-offs, follow-up work, what it makes harder>

## Scope
small | medium | large, and matching `scope:` label
```

## Issue format: bug report

Template: `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug-report.yaml`.

```markdown
## Observed Behavior
## Expected Behavior
## Steps to Reproduce
1. ...
## Additional Information
<Version or commit, browser/OS, logs, screenshots.>
## Design Decision
<Same four fields as above: Decision, Alternatives Considered, Rationale, Consequences.>
```

- **Design Decision (D3):** fill it in once you've picked an approach, before opening the PR. Put
  a second decision under another `### Decision 2` heading. If a PR changes the decision, update
  the issue body.
- **Peer review (D2):** a teammate reads the spec and comments `Spec reviewed — <notes>` on the
  issue before implementation starts.

## Pull request format

Template: `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Title uses Conventional Commits, e.g.
`fix(issues): keep label filter after search`. Description sections:

1. `Closes #<N>`, which links the issue and closes it on merge.
2. **What changed:** the change in your own words.
3. **Why:** the problem, and which acceptance criteria (AC1…) it satisfies.
4. **How it was tested / Test strategy:** tests added or updated and why these ones. Name any
   change that can't be tested automatically and how it was checked by hand. Every behaviour change
   needs a new or updated test.
5. **CI / manual verification:** CI status, or the commands run and their results.
6. **Design:** one line pointing at the Design Decision in the issue, or a note on how it changed.
7. **Tech Debt:** required from Sprint 2. Both fields are required, and `None.` is a valid answer:

   ```markdown
   ## Tech Debt

   **Introduced:** <shortcuts, workarounds or design compromises this PR makes, and why>

   **Encountered:** <tech debt that was already there and that you ran into, and how you handled it>
   ```

8. **AI assistance:** format in `AI-ASSISTANCE.md` §2, with **no log link**.

Per-PR grading (20 points): correctness against the acceptance criteria 6, test strategy with
explanation 5, description quality including the Tech Debt section 4, CI or manual verification 3,
review rubric posted 2.

## Code review rubric

The reviewer posts this as a **PR comment**, as well as the GitHub review itself. A copy-paste copy
is in `.github/code-review-rubric.md`, so keep the two in sync. Pull the branch and test it when you
can, say what you checked, and mark each point as required or optional
(`docs/community-governance.md`). Score each row against the issue's acceptance criteria. Anything
below 7 needs a note saying what would raise it.

```markdown
### Code Review — @reviewer-username

**Checked:** <what you ran or tried>
```

import {throttle} from 'throttle-debounce';
import {addDelegatedEventListener, generateElemId, isDocumentFragmentOrElementNode} from '../utils/dom.ts';
import octiconKebabHorizontal from '../../../public/assets/img/svg/octicon-kebab-horizontal.svg';

window.customElements.define('overflow-menu', class extends HTMLElement {
  popup!: HTMLDivElement;
  overflowItems: Array<HTMLElement> = [];
  button: HTMLButtonElement | null = null;
  menuItemsEl!: HTMLElement;
  resizeObserver!: ResizeObserver;
  mutationObserver!: MutationObserver;
  lastWidth!: number;

  updateButtonActivationState() {
    if (!this.button || !this.popup) return;
    this.button.classList.toggle('active', Boolean(this.popup.querySelector('.item.active')));
  }

  showPopup() {
    if (!this.popup || this.popup.style.display !== 'none') return;
    this.popup.style.display = '';
    this.button!.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
    setTimeout(() => this.popup.focus(), 0);
    document.addEventListener('click', this.onClickOutside, {capture: true});
  }

  hidePopup() {
    if (!this.popup || this.popup.style.display === 'none') return;
    this.popup.style.display = 'none';
    this.button?.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
    document.removeEventListener('click', this.onClickOutside, true);
  }

  onClickOutside = (e: Event) => {
    if (!this.popup?.contains(e.target as Node) && !this.button?.contains(e.target as Node)) {
      this.hidePopup();
    }
  };

  updateItems = throttle(100, () => {
    if (!this.popup) {
      const div = document.createElement('div');
      div.classList.add('overflow-menu-popup');
      div.setAttribute('role', 'menu');
      div.tabIndex = -1; // for initial focus, programmatic focus only
      div.style.display = 'none';
      div.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => {
        if (e.isComposing) return;
        if (e.key === 'Tab') {
          const items = this.popup.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('[role="menuitem"]');
          if (e.shiftKey) {
            if (document.activeElement === items[0]) {
              e.preventDefault();
              items[items.length - 1].focus();
            }
          } else {
            if (document.activeElement === items[items.length - 1]) {
              e.preventDefault();
              items[0].focus();
            }
          }
        } else if (e.key === 'Escape') {
          e.preventDefault();
          e.stopPropagation();
          this.hidePopup();
          this.button?.focus();
        } else if (e.key === ' ' || e.code === 'Enter') {
          if (document.activeElement?.matches('[role="menuitem"]')) {
            e.preventDefault();
            e.stopPropagation();
            (document.activeElement as HTMLElement).click();
          }
        } else if (e.key === 'ArrowDown') {
          if (document.activeElement === this.popup) {
            e.preventDefault();
            e.stopPropagation();
            this.popup.querySelector<HTMLElement>('[role="menuitem"]:first-of-type')?.focus();
          } else if (document.activeElement?.matches('[role="menuitem"]')) {
            e.preventDefault();
            e.stopPropagation();
            (document.activeElement.nextElementSibling as HTMLElement)?.focus();
          }
        } else if (e.key === 'ArrowUp') {
          if (document.activeElement === this.popup) {
            e.preventDefault();
            e.stopPropagation();
            this.popup.querySelector<HTMLElement>('[role="menuitem"]:last-of-type')?.focus();
          } else if (document.activeElement?.matches('[role="menuitem"]')) {
            e.preventDefault();
            e.stopPropagation();
            (document.activeElement.previousElementSibling as HTMLElement)?.focus();
          }
        }
      });
      this.handleItemClick(div, '.overflow-menu-popup > .item');
      this.popup = div;
    } // end if: no popup and create a new one

    const itemFlexSpace = this.menuItemsEl.querySelector<HTMLSpanElement>('.item-flex-space');
    const itemOverFlowMenuButton = this.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>('.overflow-menu-button');

    // move items in popup back into the menu items for subsequent measurement
    for (const item of this.overflowItems) {
      if (!itemFlexSpace || item.getAttribute('data-after-flex-space')) {
        this.menuItemsEl.append(item);
      } else {

- **`make lint-go` stops on `modules/options/options_bindata.go: pattern bindata.dat: no matching
  files found (typecheck)`.** `tools/lint-go-all.go` always lints with `--build-tags=linux,bindata`,
  and `bindata.dat` is a generated, untracked asset. Unrelated to any change; the header step before
  it still runs. Scoped substitute that works: `golangci-lint run --build-tags=linux <pkgs>`.
  (Seen 2026-09-27.)
- **`specstory sync` does not work in this setup** (user, 2026-09-27). Don't remind them to run it
  at wrap-up, despite `AGENTS.md`; they handle AI logs themselves.
- **`make lint-json` fails on `data/indexers/issues.bleve/index_meta.json`** — a runtime file from
  running Gitea locally, in the gitignored `/data`. Not a repo problem; lint the file you changed
  alone: `pnpm exec eslint -c eslint.json.config.ts --max-warnings=0 <file>`. (Seen 2026-09-27.)
- **(Resolved by 2026-09-27: `~/sdk/go1.26.4/bin` is now first on `PATH`.) Local Go was newer than
  the repo's.** `go.mod` pins `go 1.26.4` (CI uses `go-version-file: go.mod`)
  but the system Go is 1.27.0. Two symptoms: `make fmt` silently rewrites `modules/git/key.go`
  (1.27's gofmt re-indents composite literals in multi-value returns), and `make lint-go` *panics*
  rather than reporting findings — `buildir: package "poll" ... unexpected expr: *ast.KeyValueExpr`,
  staticcheck v0.7.0 choking on the 1.27 stdlib. Scoping the lint to one package does not help;
  `internal/poll` is a transitive dep of `net/http`. Fix: `go install golang.org/dl/go1.26.4@latest`,
  `go1.26.4 download`, and put `~/sdk/go1.26.4/bin` first on `PATH`.
- **`~/go/bin` is not on `PATH`.** `tools/lint-go-all.go` does `go install` then execs the bare name,
  so `make lint-go` dies with `exec: "golangci-lint": executable file not found in $PATH`.
- **openSUSE**, so `zypper`. `uv` (needed by `make lint-templates`) is packaged as `python313-uv`,
  though it also `Provides: uv`.
- **The VS Code integrated terminal cannot paste**, images included, so `Ctrl+V` into the prompt
  does not work. Screenshots land in `~/Pictures/Screenshots/`, and reads outside the working
  directory are blocked — `cp` the file into the scratchpad first, then read it from there.
- **Prettier with `editor.formatOnSave` fights the repo's linters** (eslint `@stylistic`, stylelint,
  the JSON check). A gitignored `.vscode/settings.json` disables format-on-save per language, runs
  `eslint --fix` on save instead, and maps `*.tmpl` to HTML for highlighting.

**Why:** each of these cost real time once. The Go mismatch is the worst because it fails as an
unrelated dirty file and a stack trace, neither of which points at the cause.

**How to apply:** if `make lint-go` panics or `make fmt` touches a file you never opened, check
`go version` against `go.mod` before reading the error. Scoped alternatives that work on 1.27:
`golangci-lint fmt <pkg>`, `go vet <pkg>`, `go test <pkg>`. Note `make lint-editorconfig` only
covers `templates .github/workflows options/locale/locale_en-US.json` (`Makefile:144`) — it does not
check `routers/` or new non-Go files. Related: [[prefers-make-targets]].

- The tab bar starts at `templates/repo/header.tmpl:83`, and a tab only exists on the page when it's shown.
- The external issue tracker and external wiki are separate links that open in a new tab.
- In a narrow window, `web_src/js/webcomponents/overflow-menu.ts` moves those same links into the "more" popup, which stays on the page.

The options:
- **(a) Mark the tab links in the template**, the way #56's `S`/`T` hints mark themselves. Each shown tab registers its own shortcut and goes where it links:
  - A hidden tab has no shortcut (AC3, AC7).
  - The external tabs just don't get marked (AC4).
  - The "more" menu moves a link but keeps it on the page, so its shortcut keeps working (AC5).
  - `g c` is the one exception. It carries the repo's front page as its own URL and ignores where the tab links (AC2).
- **(b) The server passes the page a list of URLs.** The rules for which tabs are shown would then be written twice, once in the template and once in Go, and the two could drift apart.
- **(c) JS builds fixed paths, like the repo link + `/issues`.** JS can't tell which tabs are shown, so to pass AC3 and AC4 it would have to check the tab bar anyway. That's (a) with extra steps.

I recommend **(a)**. One consequence: the notifications bell (`templates/base/head_navbar_icons.tmpl:14`) is on the page twice, once for the phone layout and once for desktop. Only one copy can be marked, or #56's clash check throws an error.

Are you OK with (a)? If so, I'll write it up in plain language in `.specstory/issue-58-design-decisions.md` and plan the first commit.

It's twice in the HTML, and only one is ever displayed. There are never two bells stacked on top of each other.

`templates/base/head_navbar.tmpl` includes the bell template twice:
- **Line 10**, inside `navbar-mobile-right only-mobile`: the phone layout's bell.
- **Line 65**, with the `not-mobile` class: the desktop bell.

`web_src/css/helpers.css:33-43` hides one of them with `display: none` depending on the window width. Below 768px you see the phone copy, and above that you see the desktop copy. Both stay in the DOM the whole time.

That matters for #58 because #56's registry only checks whether an element is *on the page* (`isConnected`), not whether it's *displayed*. That's the "counts as present even when hidden" item in #96's Tech Debt section. If both bells were marked, `g n` would be registered twice on every page, and the clash check would throw. So only one copy gets marked. Both are always in the HTML, so `g n` works at any window width whichever one we pick.

```text
## Design Decision for Commit 1 - @ab-wm

### Decision 1: Shortcuts are kept in one list in the page code, and a shortcut can belong to a part of the page

**Decision:** Shortcuts are added to a single list in the page code, each with its keys, a description and an optional section, and one key handler serves them all. A shortcut can belong to a part of the page, such as the search box its `S` hint sits beside, and only exists while that part is on the page.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) Keep the page's HTML as the list, as today: on each key press, look for a hint showing that key. (b) Have whatever adds a shortcut remove it again when its part of the page goes away. (c) Let the newest shortcut for a key replace the older one.
**Rationale:** (a) can't hold a shortcut that has no box to focus, like `?` or `g c`. (b) would need a new way to notice removals, since the file tree swaps the page content without tearing anything down; checking whether the part of the page is still there is simpler and costs nothing until a key is pressed. (c) would let two shortcuts on the same key pass silently, which AC8 rules out. Tying a shortcut to its part of the page lets a hint that the file tree reloads come back without an error, and keeps the list accurate after moving around.
**Consequences:** Adding a shortcut is one call, and shortcuts with no box become possible. A part of the page that is hidden but not removed still counts as present, so #58 and #59 must tie their shortcuts to something that gets removed, or check for themselves. Finding out what a key does now means looking at the list in the code as well as the HTML.

## Design Decision for Commit 3 - @ab-wm

### Decision 2: Each hint names its own section in the page's HTML

**Decision:** A hint states its translated section ("Repository") on itself, beside the key it already declares. The "Go to file" box receives it the same way it already receives its placeholder text.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) A hint takes its section from the part of the page it sits in, declared once on a surrounding element. (b) Send the section names to every page along with the few general strings Gitea already gives the page code.
**Rationale:** (a) needs fewer edits, but a hint's section would depend on markup far away from it, and moving a hint could silently change its section. (b) is reserved for general text by a comment where it is set up. Declaring it on the hint keeps everything about a shortcut in one place, and follows how Gitea already hands translated text to page code: tooltips, confirm dialogs and the file finder's own placeholder each use an attribute named for what it holds.
**Consequences:** A new hint that forgets its section is listed without one. The "Go to file" box gains one more setting passed through to it. The existing "Repository" string is reused, so it is already translated. Shortcuts added from code give their section directly, so this only concerns hints.
```

```text
import {isDocumentFragmentOrElementNode} from '../utils/dom.ts';
import type {Promisable} from '../types.ts';
import type {InitPerformanceTracer} from './init.ts';
import {initAriaLabels} from './fomantic/base.ts';

let globalSelectorObserverInited = false;

type SelectorHandler<T extends Element> = {selector: string, handler: (el: T) => void};
const selectorHandlers: SelectorHandler<Element>[] = [];

type GlobalEventFunc<T extends HTMLElement, E extends Event> = (el: T, e: E) => Promisable<void>;
const globalEventFuncs: Record<string, GlobalEventFunc<HTMLElement, Event>> = {};

type GlobalInitFunc<T extends Element> = (el: T) => Promisable<void>;
const globalInitFuncs: Record<string, GlobalInitFunc<Element>> = {};

// It handles the global events for all `<div data-global-click="onSomeElemClick"></div>` elements.
export function registerGlobalEventFunc<T extends HTMLElement, E extends Event>(event: string, name: string, func: GlobalEventFunc<T, E>) {
  globalEventFuncs[`${event}:${name}`] = func as GlobalEventFunc<HTMLElement, Event>;
}

// It handles the global init functions by a selector, for example:
// > registerGlobalSelectorObserver('.ui.dropdown:not(.custom)', (el) => { initDropdown(el, ...) });
// ATTENTION: For most cases, it's recommended to use registerGlobalInitFunc instead,
// Because this selector-based approach is less efficient and less maintainable.
// But if there are already a lot of elements on many pages, this selector-based approach is more convenient for exiting code.
export function registerGlobalSelectorFunc<T extends Element>(selector: string, handler: (el: T) => void) {
  selectorHandlers.push({selector, handler: handler as (el: Element) => void});
  // Then initAddedElementObserver will call this handler for all existing elements after all handlers are added.
  // This approach makes the init stage only need to do one "querySelectorAll".
  if (!globalSelectorObserverInited) return;
  for (const el of document.querySelectorAll<T>(selector)) {
    handler(el);
  }
}

// It handles the global init functions for all `<div data-global-int="initSomeElem"></div>` elements.
export function registerGlobalInitFunc<T extends HTMLElement>(name: string, handler: GlobalInitFunc<T>) {
  globalInitFuncs[name] = handler as GlobalInitFunc<Element>;
  // The "global init" functions are managed internally and called by callGlobalInitFunc
  // They must be ready before initGlobalSelectorObserver is called.
  if (globalSelectorObserverInited) throw new Error('registerGlobalInitFunc() must be called before initGlobalSelectorObserver()');
}

function callGlobalInitFunc(el: Element) {
  // TODO: GLOBAL-INIT-MULTIPLE-FUNCTIONS: maybe in the future we need to extend it to support multiple functions, for example: `data-global-init="func1 func2 func3"`
  const initFunc = el.getAttribute('data-global-init')!;
  const func = globalInitFuncs[initFunc];
  if (!func) throw new Error(`Global init function "${initFunc}" not found`);

  // when an element node is removed and added again, it should not be re-initialized again.
  type GiteaGlobalInitElement = Partial<Element> & {_giteaGlobalInited: boolean};
  if ((el as GiteaGlobalInitElement)._giteaGlobalInited) return;
  (el as GiteaGlobalInitElement)._giteaGlobalInited = true;

  func(el);
}

function attachGlobalEvents() {
  // add global "[data-global-click]" event handler
  document.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
    const elem = (e.target as HTMLElement).closest<HTMLElement>('[data-global-click]');
    if (!elem) return;
    const funcName = elem.getAttribute('data-global-click');
    const func = globalEventFuncs[`click:${funcName}`];
    if (!func) throw new Error(`Global event function "click:${funcName}" not found`);
    func(elem, e);
  });
}

export function initGlobalSelectorObserver(perfTracer: InitPerformanceTracer | null): void {
  if (globalSelectorObserverInited) throw new Error('initGlobalSelectorObserver() already called');
  globalSelectorObserverInited = true;

  attachGlobalEvents();

  selectorHandlers.push({selector: '[data-global-init]', handler: callGlobalInitFunc});
  const observer = new MutationObserver((mutationList) => {
    const len = mutationList.length;
    for (let i = 0; i < len; i++) {
      const mutation = mutationList[i];
      const len = mutation.addedNodes.length;
      for (let i = 0; i < len; i++) {
        const addedNode = mutation.addedNodes[i] as ParentNode;
        if (!isDocumentFragmentOrElementNode(addedNode)) continue;

        initAriaLabels(addedNode);
        for (const {selector, handler} of selectorHandlers) {
          if ((addedNode instanceof Element) && addedNode.matches(selector)) {
            handler(addedNode);
          }
          for (const el of addedNode.querySelectorAll?.<HTMLElement>(selector) ?? []) {
            handler(el);
          }
        }
      }
    }
  });

  initAriaLabels(document);
  if (perfTracer) {
    for (const {selector, handler} of selectorHandlers) {
      perfTracer.recordCall(`initGlobalSelectorObserver ${selector}`, () => {
        for (const el of document.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>(selector)) {
          handler(el);
        }
      });
    }
  } else {
    for (const {selector, handler} of selectorHandlers) {
      for (const el of document.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>(selector)) {
        handler(el);
      }
    }
  }
  observer.observe(document, {subtree: true, childList: true});
}

import {ShortcutRegistry, getShortcuts, initGlobalShortcut, initShortcutKbd} from './shortcut.ts';

function setup() {
  const registry = new ShortcutRegistry();
  const root = document.createElement('div');
  root.innerHTML = `
    <button type="button">button</button>
    <input><textarea></textarea><select></select><div contenteditable="true"></div>
  `;
  root.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => registry.handleKeyDown(e));
  document.body.append(root);
  const button = root.querySelector('button')!;
  const add = (keys: string, opts: {element?: HTMLElement} = {}) => {
    const action = vi.fn();
    registry.register({keys, description: `run ${keys}`, action, ...opts});
    return action;
  };
  return {registry, root, button, add, cleanup: () => root.remove()};
}

function press(el: Element, key: string, opts: KeyboardEventInit = {}): KeyboardEvent {
  const e = new KeyboardEvent('keydown', {key, bubbles: true, cancelable: true, ...opts});
  el.dispatchEvent(e);
  return e;
}

// these tests share document.body and fake timers, so they must not run concurrently (see vitest.config.ts)

  let ctx: ReturnType<typeof setup>;
  beforeEach(() => {
    vi.useFakeTimers();
    ctx = setup();
  });
  afterEach(() => {
    ctx.cleanup();
    vi.useRealTimers();

    press(ctx.button, 'Shift', {shiftKey: true});

// the markup of templates/repo/home_sidebar_top.tmpl and RepoFileSearch.vue
function renderHint(key: string, placeholder: string, section?: string) {
  const wrapper = document.createElement('div');
  wrapper.className = 'ui input global-shortcut-wrapper';
  wrapper.innerHTML = `<input placeholder="${placeholder}"><kbd data-shortcut-keys="${key}">${key.toUpperCase()}</kbd>`;
  document.body.append(wrapper);
  const input = wrapper.querySelector('input')!;
  const kbd = wrapper.querySelector('kbd')!;
  if (section) kbd.setAttribute('data-shortcut-section', section);
  initShortcutKbd(kbd);
  return {wrapper, input, kbd};
}
```

```markdown
## Design Decision for Commit 1 - @ab-wm

### Decision 1: Each tab's link in the tab bar declares its own `g` shortcut

**Decision:** The tab bar's links declare their shortcuts in the page's HTML, and a shortcut goes where its link leads. The one exception is `g c`, which goes to the repository's front page instead of the branch the Code tab points at. The notifications bell declares `g n` the same way.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) The server works out which tabs the user may open and hands the page a list of their addresses. (b) The page code builds each address from the repository's address, for example by adding `/issues`.
**Rationale:** The tab bar already decides which tabs to show. It leaves out a tab whose feature is turned off, one the user cannot read, and Actions on an empty repository, and it shows an outside link for an external tracker or wiki. Declaring the shortcut on the tab means a shortcut exists exactly when its tab does, so AC3, AC4 and AC7 need no rules of their own. (a) would repeat the tab bar's rules in a second place, where they could drift apart. (b) cannot tell which tabs are shown, so it would send users to pages they cannot open, or have to look at the tab bar anyway. On a narrow window, tabs that no longer fit move into the "more" menu but stay on the page, so their shortcuts keep working (AC5).
**Consequences:** A `g` shortcut for another tab later takes a few attributes on its link. Each shortcut's description is given separately, because a tab's text also holds its open count. The bell is in the HTML twice, once for small screens and once for large ones, so only one copy declares `g n`, or the two would clash. `g c` carries its own address, because following the Code tab would keep the user on the branch they are browsing (AC2).

```

Decision 1 is written up, and commit 1 is ready in the sandbox for you to review.

**Decision 1** is in `.specstory/issue-58-design-decisions.md`, under "Design Decision for Commit 1", in your #56 format. If you keep your own copy like `decisions.md` last time, tell me its name and I'll keep both in step.

**The plan for #58.** Only commit 1 is built; the rest is a sketch, and we'll take them one at a time:
1. **This one:** a link can declare a shortcut that goes where it leads. The code and tests are written, but no page uses it yet.
2. `g i`, `g p`, `g a`, `g w` on the tab bar.
3. `g c`, which needs its own address.
4. `g n` on the bell. This needs a decision on which section it's listed under, since #57's "General" heading doesn't exist yet.
5. Playwright tests on real pages.
6. `.claude-students` docs.

**Commit 1: what changed and why**
- **`web_src/js/modules/shortcut.ts`:** a new `initShortcutLink` sits next to `initShortcutKbd` and is registered as `onShortcutLink`. It uses the same `data-global-init` hook as the `S`/`T` hints.
  - It reuses `data-shortcut-keys` and `data-shortcut-section` from #56. It also adds `data-shortcut-description`, because a tab's own text includes its open count (AC8).
  - Its action is `window.location.assign(link.href)`. `web_src/js` already navigates this way in 8 other places.
- **Why the "more" menu works (AC5):** `web_src/js/modules/observer.ts:47-50` marks an element once it has been set up. When the overflow menu moves a tab, the tab doesn't register a second time, so there's no clash error.
- **`shortcut.test.ts`:** three new tests.
  - They're named `#58 AC1/AC5/AC8`, because the bare `ACn` names in that file belong to #56, and #57 will add its own.
  - I renamed the hint `describe` to "shortcut hints and links" so the new tests share its `beforeAll`. A second `initGlobalShortcut()` call would add a second key listener and run every shortcut twice.
  - The AC5 test moves the link into a *hidden* menu, as when the "more" menu is closed. That way it fails if anyone later decides hidden means gone.

**Checked**
- 22/22 unit tests pass, and `make lint-js` passes.
- I broke the code four ways: description taken from the link text, section dropped, action does nothing, hidden counted as gone. A test failed for each.

Commit 2 is ready. It's a template-only change, and I tried it on a real page.

**What changed:** `templates/repo/header.tmpl`. The Issues, Pull Requests, Actions and Wiki tab links each get four attributes:
- `data-global-init="onShortcutLink"` sets the link up through commit 1's code.
- `data-shortcut-keys="g i"` (and `g p`, `g a`, `g w`).
- `data-shortcut-description` uses the same locale key as the tab's own label (`repo.issues`, `repo.pulls`, `actions.actions`, `repo.wiki`), so it's already translated and has no count (AC8).
- `data-shortcut-section` uses `"repository"`, the same key as the `S`/`T` hints, so all repository shortcuts end up in one section.

I left these alone on purpose:
- **External tracker and external wiki tabs:** not marked, so `g i`/`g w` simply don't exist there (AC4).
- **Code tab:** it's commit 3.
- **Projects, Releases, Packages, Activity, Settings:** out of scope per the spec.

The attributes go on the existing tag line, as on the `S` hint in `home_sidebar_top.tmpl`. The lines are long, but `.editorconfig` has no length limit and 35 template lines are already longer than 200 characters.

**Checked**
- `make lint-templates` passes.
- **On a real page:** the sandbox now has its own server on **http://localhost:3001**, so you can try the keys yourself. It uses a copy of your `app.ini` inside the sandbox (gitignored), with your dev database, and it's running in the background. A headless Chromium run against `abhoot/tjyjy` passed 8/8:
  - `g i`, `g p`, `g a`, `g w` go to their tabs (AC1).
  - At 420px wide, the Wiki tab is in the "more" menu and `g w` still works (AC5).
  - `g i` on `/explore/repos` does nothing (AC7).
  - No JS errors.
- Not checked yet: AC3/AC4. Those need repos with units turned off, and the Playwright commit (5) will create them.

```text
- **Only ever edit `locale_en-US.json`.** Every other locale file is written by Crowdin
  (`crowdin.yml` sets `en-US` as the source). Editing one by hand is overwritten on the next sync,
  and a PR that touches other locale files will be asked to revert them.
- Keys are dotted and grouped by area (`repo.issues.new`, `settings.`, `admin.`). Put a new key
  next to its neighbours rather than at the end.
- Templates use `{{ctx.Locale.Tr "key"}}`, or `TrN` for plurals. TypeScript uses `trN` from
  `web_src/js/modules/i18n.ts`; strings reach the frontend through `window.config.i18n`
  (`templates/base/head_script.tmpl`), which is deliberately limited to general text — anything
  specialised should arrive via an API response, a `data-` attribute, or `pageData`.
- A plural is **two keys** suffixed `_1` and `_n`, both interpolating `%d` — see
  `actions.runs.graph_jobs_count_1` and `_n`. `TrN` and `trN` pick the form from the count.
- A `data-` attribute carrying a translated string to TypeScript is read with `getAttribute` and
  usually named for its use (`data-tooltip-content`, read in `web_src/js/modules/tippy.ts`). Vue
  mounts often use `data-locale-<name>`, as `templates/repo/actions/view_component.tmpl` does for
  both plural forms.
- **Never write a user-visible literal** in a template, a handler, or a `.ts` file.
- Errors whose message reaches the user go through `util.ErrorWrapTranslatable`
  (`modules-util-and-generics.md`), not a plain `fmt.Errorf`.
- `crowdin.yml` sets `skip_untranslated_strings` and `export_only_approved`, so a missing
  translation falls back rather than shipping an empty string.

## Gotchas

- A missing key renders as the key itself — visible in the UI but easy to miss on a rarely-hit
  branch.
- Changing an existing key's *text* is fine; changing the *key name* invalidates every existing
  translation for it.
- Only a `bindata` build embeds `options/locale` (`modules/options/options_bindata.go`) and needs a
  rebuild for a locale change. A plain build reads the files from disk at startup
  (`modules/options/options_dynamic.go`), and outside `RUN_MODE = prod` reloads them on change
  (`modules/translation/translation.go` → `WatchLocalChanges`).
- Some keys are built from an enum's name while rendering: `actions.status.%s`
```
</details></tool-use>

This matches AC8 as written, and gives one heading and one translation. It needs a quick message to your teammate (controlled-opposition) agreeing on the key name, e.g. `shortcuts.general`. They'll probably want `shortcuts.title` and similar for the dialog anyway.
- **(b) Reuse an existing "General" string**, such as `settings.general` or `actions.general`. No new string, but it borrows text that translators wrote for the settings pages. If a language words that tab differently, the shortcut list inherits it.
- **(c) No section for `g n`.** It's listed without one, and #57's dialog decides where to put shortcuts that have none. No new string, but `?` would be "General" while `g n` has no section. #57 would then need a rule its spec doesn't state, merging no-section shortcuts into "General", and AC8's "site-wide section" becomes a matter of interpretation.

I recommend **(a)**. It's the only option where `getShortcuts()` itself says `g n` is in the same section as `?`, and it costs one message to your teammate.

import {env} from 'node:process';
import {test, expect} from '@playwright/test';
import type {Page} from '@playwright/test';
import {apiCreateFile, apiCreateRepo, assertNoJsError, randomString} from './utils.ts';

async function createRepo(page: Page) {
  const repoName = `e2e-shortcut-${randomString(8)}`;
  await apiCreateRepo(page.request, {name: repoName});
  await apiCreateFile(page.request, env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_USER, repoName, 'other.txt', 'other file');
  return `/${env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_USER}/${repoName}`;
}

test('s and t focus their boxes, and Escape clears them', async ({page}) => {
  await page.goto(await createRepo(page));
  const search = page.locator('.repo-home-sidebar-top input[name="q"]');
  const searchHint = page.locator('.repo-home-sidebar-top kbd');
  const goToFile = page.locator('.repo-file-search-container input');
  const goToFileHint = page.locator('.repo-file-search-container kbd');
  await expect(goToFileHint).toHaveAttribute('aria-keyshortcuts', 't'); // the Vue box has mounted and registered
  await expect(searchHint).toHaveAttribute('data-shortcut-section', 'Repository');
  await expect(goToFileHint).toHaveAttribute('data-shortcut-section', 'Repository');

  await page.keyboard.press('s');
  await expect(search).toBeFocused();
  await expect(searchHint).toBeHidden();
  await page.keyboard.type('st');
  await expect(search).toHaveValue('st');
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
  await expect(search).toHaveValue('');
  await expect(search).not.toBeFocused();

});

  }
  await assertNoJsError(page);
});

export async function login(page: Page, username = env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_USER, password = env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_PASSWORD) {
  const response = await page.request.post('/user/login', {

  });
  const status = response.status();
  if (status !== 302 && status !== 303) throw new Error(`login as ${username} failed: HTTP ${status}`);
}

/* asserts the child has no horizontal inset from its parent — catches padding/border anywhere
 * in between regardless of which element declares it */
export async function assertFlushWithParent(child: Locator, parent: Locator) {
  const [childBox, parentBox] = await Promise.all([child.boundingBox(), parent.boundingBox()]);
  if (!childBox || !parentBox) throw new Error('boundingBox returned null');
  expect(childBox.x).toBe(parentBox.x);
  expect(childBox.width).toBe(parentBox.width);
}

}

import {env} from 'node:process';
import {expect} from '@playwright/test';
import type {APIRequestContext, Locator, Page} from '@playwright/test';

/** Generate a random alphanumeric string. */
export function randomString(length: number): string {
  const chars = 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789';
  let result = '';
  for (let index = 0; index < length; index++) {
    result += chars.charAt(Math.floor(Math.random() * chars.length));
  }
  return result;
}

export const timeoutFactor = Number(env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_TIMEOUT_FACTOR) || 1;

export function baseUrl() {
  return env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_URL?.replace(/\/$/g, '');
}

function apiAuthHeader(username: string, password: string) {
  return {Authorization: `Basic ${globalThis.btoa(`${username}:${password}`)}`};
}

export function apiHeaders() {
  return apiAuthHeader(env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_USER, env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_PASSWORD);
}

async function apiRetry(fn: () => Promise<{ok: () => boolean; status: () => number; text: () => Promise<string>}>, label: string) {
  const maxAttempts = 5;
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < maxAttempts; attempt++) {
    const response = await fn();
    if (response.ok()) return;
    if ([500, 502, 503].includes(response.status()) && attempt < maxAttempts - 1) {
      const jitter = Math.random() * 500;
      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 1000 * (attempt + 1) + jitter));
      continue;
    }
    throw new Error(`${label} failed: ${response.status()} ${await response.text()}`);
  }
}

export async function apiCreateRepo(requestContext: APIRequestContext, {name, autoInit = true, headers}: {name: string; autoInit?: boolean; headers?: Record<string, string>}) {
  await apiRetry(() => requestContext.post(`${baseUrl()}/api/v1/user/repos`, {
    headers: headers || apiHeaders(),
    data: {name, auto_init: autoInit},
  }), 'apiCreateRepo');
}

export async function apiCreateOrg(requestContext: APIRequestContext, name: string, {headers}: {headers?: Record<string, string>} = {}) {
  }), 'createProjectColumn');
}

export async function apiDeleteRepo(requestContext: APIRequestContext, owner: string, name: string) {
  await apiRetry(() => requestContext.delete(`${baseUrl()}/api/v1/repos/${owner}/${name}`, {
    headers: apiHeaders(),
  }), 'apiDeleteRepo');
}

## Conventions & invariants

**Two ways to wire a feature, and new code should prefer the second.**
number comes back first (`services/issue/suggestion.go` → `GetSuggestion`), and the current issue
is left out. Keyword matches are limited to the kinds the viewer may read
(`routers/web/repo/issue_suggestions.go`), but the match by number (`GetIssueByIndex`) is not, so a
viewer who can't read pull requests still gets one typed by its number. The duplicate close
reason's preview in `features/repo-issue-status-button.ts` uses it.

**Add a keyboard shortcut.** Call `registerShortcut` (`modules/shortcut.ts`). One given an `element`
exists while that element is in the document, hidden or not; a clash with a live one throws.

**Run one test file.** `pnpm exec vitest <path-filter>` (`testing.md`).

## Gotchas

- Forgetting the early return in a page-load init means that feature's cost is paid on every page
  in Gitea, which is what the 500ms warning is there to catch.
- Fomantic-UI (jQuery) is vendored and deprecated. Do not build new features on it, and do not mix
  it with Vue — Vue may use its CSS classes but not its JavaScript.
- Which menu to build on, Fomantic dropdown or `<aria-menu>` (`web_src/js/webcomponents/aria-menu.ts`),
  is decided in `web_src/js/modules/fomantic/aria.md`.
- `utils/` is for pure helpers. A function that reaches for `window` or a global selector belongs
  in `modules/` or `features/`.

## The guide layer (rules 16-22)

`guide/` holds a plain-English page for each reference page in `docs/`, same filename. It exists so
a person new to Go and to this codebase can get oriented. It is **derived**, not independent.

16. Every guide carries `source:`, `source-hash:` and `verified-at:` in its frontmatter **[checked]**.
17. A guide's `source:` names a real `docs/*.md` with the **same filename** **[checked]**.
18. `source-hash:` is the first 16 characters of `sha256sum docs/<name>.md`. If the reference page
    changes and the guide is not regenerated, `check.sh` reports **drift** **[checked]**. Regenerating
    means: reread the reference page, rewrite the guide, update the hash and `verified-at`.
19. Guide headings match `guide/_TEMPLATE.md` exactly and in order **[checked]**.
20. Guides are capped at **200 lines**, code fences at **30** **[checked]** — teaching needs more room
    than reference does.
21. **A guide adds explanation, vocabulary and worked steps. It adds no new facts.** Every repo path
    a guide cites must also be cited by its source page **[checked]**. If you need a fact the
    reference page lacks, add it *there* first, which bumps the hash and forces the guide to be
    regenerated in the same commit — exactly the intended order.
22. `guide/START-HERE.md` has no source page. It is exempt from rules 17, 18 and 21, and is where
    cross-cutting material lives that no single reference page owns.

**Never fix a fact in `guide/`.** If the two layers disagree, the reference page is the truth and
the guide is stale: fix `docs/`, regenerate the guide, ship both in one PR. A disagreement is a bug
report against `docs/`, not an editing job in `guide/`.
